This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test case fails when reading a CPIO archive generated by Redline RPM. The issue report indicates that Redline RPM creates CPIO archives with a non-zero file mode on the trailer entry, which is against the expected behavior.

Inspecting `CpioArchiveInputStream.getNextCPIOEntry`, we see it reads entries until it encounters the special trailer entry (`CPIO_TRAILER`), at which point it returns null to signal the end of entries.

The critical part is in `readNewEntry(boolean hasCrc)`: after reading the mode field from the entry header, the code checks if the mode is zero. If it is zero and the entry is not the trailer (name != CPIO_TRAILER), it throws an IOException. This suggests the code expects only the trailer entry to have zero mode, while other entries should not.

However, the report states that Redline RPM creates a trailer entry with a non-zero mode, which violates this assumption. The test reading this archive causes `IllegalArgumentException` because the code later checks or relies on the mode being zero for the trailer entry.

Moreover, the snippet for `CpioArchiveEntry.getMode()` shows it returns `C_ISREG` (a default regular file mode) if mode is zero and the entry name is not the trailer, reinforcing the special treatment of the trailer entry.

Therefore, the root cause is the strict assumption in `readNewEntry()` that only the trailer entry can have zero mode and that trailer mode must be zero. Redline RPM's trailer having a non-zero mode breaks this assumption and leads to the exception.

The fix should relax the mode checks for the trailer entry to accept non-zero mode or handle this special case gracefully.

No recent bug reports directly address this same issue, so the indication comes solely from the current bug report and inspection of related methods in `CpioArchiveInputStream`.

The failure happens during the `getNextEntry()` call which delegates to `getNextCPIOEntry()`, which calls `readNewEntry()` when it identifies the newc magic header.

This matches the test case failure at the reading entries loop where `getNextEntry()` throws due to mode validation on the trailer entry.

Hence, the bug arises due to invalid assumptions about the trailer entry mode in `readNewEntry()` in `CpioArchiveInputStream`.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
